entityDescription:
The University of Greifswald is one of the oldest universities in Germany and the Baltic Sea Region. Founded in 1456, it is also the oldest Swedish university, as the region was ruled by the Swedes after the Thirty YearsWar and up until 1815.
Still today, the University of Greifswald is closely tied to the universities of the Baltic Sea Region. But now the international relationships in both research and teaching have spread to regions and countries across the globe. The University today sustains international exchange relationships to more than 200 universities. There are currently international students and scholars from more than 100 different countries.
The University of Greifswald is a research university. Its research strength mainly originates in the intensive interdisciplinary collaboration of the five faculties, including University Medicine. Cutting-edge research evolves in close collaboration with regional, national and international research partners and is based on the solid foundation provided by an excellent research infrastructure.“Challenges and solutions of a changing environment and society” is the University of Greifswald’s research mission. There are three interdepartmental and collaborating research domains,which are based on 12 very well-established interdisciplinary key research topics.
The University is at the centre of the science location that is Greifswald and works together closely with the four internationally renowned external research institutions in the town, the Federal Research Institute for Animal Health (FLI), the Leibniz Institute for Plasma Science and Technology (INP),the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP), and the Helmholtz Institute for One Health (HIOH). The University is also a benefactor of the Alfried Krupp Wissenschaftskolleg Greifswald (Institute for Advanced Studies), which supports research and teaching at the University of Greifswald by inviting national and international fellows to Greifswald for periods of research and holds conferences and lectures.
The University of Greifswald sets itself high standards for good teaching. It offers outstanding study conditions in modern buildings and arduously restored historical buildings with an excellent infrastructure for research-led teaching. Small groups and passionate teaching staff guarantee intensive supervision of the students. Five faculties offer a broad range of subjects with a total of 131 possible degree courses, several of which are interdisciplinary, and 13 continuing education courses.
A proven quality assurance system encourages the high quality of teaching through regular external and internal evaluations of the degree courses and student feedback. The University received its system accreditation in 2015 and is taking part in several audit procedures.
The University of Greifswald has a positive effect on the town and the region. It is a major catalyst for the economic and social development of the region and the state. By holding Idea Competitions and putting material and structural measures into effect, the University supports the start-up culture and the transfer of research results to the industry. At the same time, it uses its applied research to tackle specific challenges of the rural region, such as the problems regarding the provision of healthcare in structurally weak regions.
The University shapes and enriches the life and culture in the historic Hanseatic town of Greifswald with its academic ceremonies and culture festivals, student clubs and initiatives, international events, broad and diverse academic communication with the general public and its members’ high levels of active citizenship.

We also develop compact AI models and lightweight acceleration techniques that enable real time classification, prediction, and signal processing on embedded devices.

Shobolinsky maintains a compact in house research and development environment in Romania where we handle design, validation, and small batch manufacturing. This setup allows us to work efficiently and iterate quickly while maintaining professional engineering standards. Our long term goal is to grow our modular hardware and AI platforms into dependable tools for education, applied research, and early stage space related technology development. description:
EROFIO Additive is one of Europe’s most advanced metal additive manufacturing centres, integrated within EROFIO’s long-established mould-making and high-precision engineering ecosystem. The company has been incorporating metal Additive Manufacturing into its tooling processes since 2011, enabling the production of conformal-cooled mould inserts and complex functional components long before AM became mainstream.
The additive division operates multiple L-PBF systems:
•	GE Concept Laser MLINE (500 × 500 × 500 mm, 4 × 400 W) – a large-format, serial-production machine for Corrax parts.
•	Concept Laser M2 (250 × 250 × 300 mm, 400 W) – optimized for 1.2709 and Corrax inserts with conformal cooling, high-strength structures, and advanced thermal management.
•	Concept Laser M3 (350 × 250 × 200 mm, 100 W) – for fine-feature components and engraving.
The portfolio expands in 2025 with the DMG-MORI LASERTEC 30 SLM 3rd Gen, supporting AlSi10Mg, Ti6Al4V and Mar55, powered by 4 × 1000 W lasers for high productivity and multi-material capability.
EROFIO also operates a DMG-MORI LASERTEC 65 DED Hybrid (735 × 650 × 560 mm), combining 5-axis machining and DED deposition for multi-material builds, large components, functional repairs and copper-enhanced thermal systems—unique in Europe.
Engineering capabilities include CFD/rheological simulation (SIGMASOFT), structural analysis (ANSYS), and topology optimization (nTop), ensuring that moulds and technical components are fully optimized before manufacturing. Extensive post-processing—heat treatment, machining/EDM, blasting and polishing—delivers aerospace-grade quality.
Through the integration of mould-making expertise and more than a decade of AM innovation, EROFIO delivers end-to-end metal additive solutions for conformal-cooled tooling, lightweight structures, thermal components and high-precision industrial and space-grade applications.

The company has been incorporating metal Additive Manufacturing into its tooling processes since 2011, enabling the production of conformal-cooled mould inserts and complex functional components long before AM became mainstream.
The additive division operates multiple L-PBF systems:
- GE Concept Laser MLINE (500 × 500 × 500 mm, 4 × 400 W) – a large-format, serial-production machine for Corrax parts.
- Concept Laser M2 (250 × 250 × 300 mm, 400 W) – optimized for 1.2709 and Corrax inserts with conformal cooling, high-strength structures, and advanced thermal management.
- Concept Laser M3 (350 × 250 × 200 mm, 100 W) – for fine-feature components and engraving.
The portfolio expands in 2025 with the DMG-MORI LASERTEC 30 SLM 3rd Gen, supporting AlSi10Mg, Ti6Al4V and Mar55, powered by 4 × 1000 W lasers for high productivity and multi-material capability.
EROFIO also operates a DMG-MORI LASERTEC 65 DED Hybrid (735 × 650 × 560 mm), combining 5-axis machining and DED deposition for multi-material builds, large components, functional repairs and copper-enhanced thermal systems—unique in Europe.
Engineering capabilities include CFD/rheological simulation (SIGMASOFT), structural analysis (ANSYS), and topology optimization (nTop), ensuring that moulds and technical components are fully optimized before manufacturing. Extensive post-processing—heat treatment, machining/EDM, blasting and polishing—delivers aerospace-grade quality.
Through the integration of mould-making expertise and more than a decade of AM innovation, EROFIO delivers end-to-end metal additive solutions for conformal-cooled tooling, lightweight structures, thermal components and high-precision industrial and space-grade applications.

description: Kili Technology is a leading enterprise-grade Training Data Management Platform (TDMP) designed to help organizations move from raw data to high-performance AI models. While many tools focus solely on "labeling," Kili positions itself as a central hub for the entire data-centric AI lifecycle: from initial curation and annotation to quality control and model iteration. For the Aerospace and Defense industry, where data is often massive, sensitive, and technically complex, Kili offers a specialized environment that addresses challenges general-purpose tools cannot. Key Differentiators for the Aerospace Industry In the aerospace sector, the "cost of error" is exceptionally high—whether it’s identifying a structural defect in a turbine or a target in satellite imagery. Kili’s platform is built around three core pillars that cater specifically to these high-stakes requirements: 1. Advanced Geospatial & High-Res Capability Aerospace projects rely heavily on Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT). Kili provides native support for ultra-high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery (including TIF and multi-spectral formats). Tiling & Performance: It can handle massive files without lag, allowing annotators to zoom into centimeter-level details (e.g., identifying specific aircraft models or infrastructure damage). Specialized Tooling: Features like Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2) integration allow for rapid, pixel-perfect masking of complex objects like runways, forests, or moving vehicles in video feeds. 2. "Defense-Grade" Security & Compliance Security is often the primary barrier for aerospace companies. Kili is one of the few platforms that offers deployment flexibility tailored for regulated environments: On-Premise & Air-Gapped: For classified missions, Kili can be deployed completely offline or within a private cloud (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government), ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the organization’s secure perimeter. Certifications: The platform is SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant, meeting the stringent data governance standards required by defense contractors and government agencies. 3. Programmatic Quality & Expert Collaboration Aerospace data often requires Subject Matter Expertise (SME)—for example, a maintenance engineer must label engine cracks, or an intelligence officer must label military hardware. Consensus & Honey-Potting: Kili uses "consensus" workflows where multiple experts label the same asset to ensure ground-truth accuracy. Programmatic QA: Instead of manual spot-checks, users can write Python scripts (via Kili’s SDK) to automatically flag anomalies, such as a "plane" labeled in the middle of an ocean, significantly reducing the "garbage in, garbage out" risk in safety-critical systems.

The non-profit foundation Urban Street Forest (USF) was founded on 19th of February 2016, registered at the Chamber of Commerce (KvK) of Amsterdam in Holland with the registry number 65388259. The foundation holds the status of a non-profit organisation (the Dutch “ANBI” status) and is accredited to the Conference of the Parties to the UNCCD (United Nations Convention to Combat Deserfication):
https://www.unccd.int/cso/urban-street-forest-foundation

The main USF objective is to plant as many trees as possible for the large-scale restoration of landscapes in countries suffering from desertification, and also in urban areas. Tree planting is preferably carried out together with local farmers involved in agroforestry projects, or local tree planting organisations.

Thanks to the planting of trees & our sponsors, USF has auto-finanzed the development of a web-app MRV platform named TreeWallet (TRL 6-7) using 100% open-source technologies, that has allowed us to register online all the single small trees that we have pianted registering its specie, photo, planting date and geo-position in whatever place of the world. Our prototype has been demonstrated in 2021-2025 with ~100 users, registering ~85.000 new trees on TreeWallet (in Spain, Holland, Morocco, Tanzania, Uganda) planting ~30 native tree species specific to each country, of which 50% are fruit trees:
https://app.treewallet.eu/public

Mission:
The mission of USF is to restore the ecological, social and economic potential of landscapes, by planting trees with local farmers, communities and partner organisations.

Vision:
We see an important role for companies to help restore degraded landscapes worldwide by supporting restorative and productive tree-planting projects. We envision a world where there is ecological, social and economic health. We see tree-planting as crucial to achieve this goal.

Strategy:
USF connects corporations and other sponsors who want to help restore landscapes/plant trees with landowners and planters in tree-planting projects, currently in the Netherlands, Spain and sub-Saharan African countries. We help corporations and other sponsors to use a sustainable approach when offsetting carbon, by steering tree-planting projects also on other environmental, social and economic benefits. USF provides accountability/proof of work of the planted trees by giving information such as the GPS location, a photo and the name of the planter, thus providing a transparent proof of work and direct connection with our planting partner on the ground.
